I’d give everything to go back. I’ve been depressed this entire weekend, willing myself on fumes. I’m honestly grateful that you wrote something real… because man… I’ve been harboring these emotions to myself. The past is in my inner peace. All the re-collections of the memories I’ve experienced with my parents and grandparents. The sunsets during a time of innocence. The slowness of the holidays. The charm of childhood innocence. The world truly seemed freer, slower, happier. When my father was passing, he told me that “we were the lucky ones.” We had each other for so long. Made so many decades of memories. The amount of love I’ve been showered with. All of us. When all you’ve know is love in the purest of forms… everything’s been so difficult since his passing in January. It feels like the life as I’d known it was gone. But I’ll forever carry that love with me. I was in a very dark place. I set out to dig deeper and show up for my kids at work and pour everything into their growth and happiness. And I’d get of work, and it’s like, I’m trying to get out a few tweets to make people laugh, but I’m exhausted. It meant more to come on here and listen to stories, DMs, or just talk. As people. And in the community playing basketball. Or at McDonald’s. Or movie theatre. Or gas station. Meeting people. Seeing their dreams, goals, ambitions. And be motivated to fight for that. To just be present. To appreciate. Love. Kindness. Hold the darn door for others. The littlest things. To see a glimmer of hope in someone’s eyes is one of the most powerful things. It was what has gotten me this far, even when it’s felt like mine has been fading Everyday shape the world around you. Give everything you’ve got. I’ve been looked over time and time again. And it hurts, when you feel like you have so much you want to give. I’ve seen a lot of “we’re in a slow burn apocalypse” vibes. But I’ve seen how that can be changed. Sheer love. It’s the most powerful thing we’ve got. It’s everything my father poured into me.
